description: Umbrella-skill knowledge used by RAG enrichment. 'indicators' are concrete sub-skills, techniques, libraries or tools that strongly imply the skill. 'not_sufficient' lists look-alike terms that must never grant credit on their own; when a not_sufficient phrase covers an indicator occurrence, that occurrence is ignored.

skills.definition: Natural language processing (NLP) is the branch of machine learning that builds systems to analyze, understand and generate human language text. Practitioners train and apply language models for tasks such as tokenization, entity recognition, text classification, summarization and translation.

Machine learning is the practice of training statistical models that learn patterns from data to make predictions or decisions without explicit rules. It covers supervised and unsupervised algorithms, feature engineering, model training and evaluation.
Deep learning is a subfield of machine learning that trains multi-layer neural networks, such as convolutional, recurrent and transformer networks, on large datasets, usually on GPUs.
Computer vision is the field of machine learning that enables computers to interpret images and video, using models for image classification, object detection, segmentation and tracking.
Reinforcement learning trains agents to choose actions that maximize cumulative reward through trial-and-error interaction with an environment.
MLOps is the discipline of deploying, monitoring and maintaining machine learning models in production, including experiment tracking, model registries, serving infrastructure and drift monitoring.
Large language model (LLM) engineering is building applications on top of large pretrained language models, including prompting, retrieval augmentation, fine-tuning and evaluation of model outputs.
Prompt engineering is designing, testing and iterating instructions and examples given to large language models so they produce reliable, well-structured outputs.

Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) combines a retriever that finds relevant documents, usually via embeddings and a vector index, with a language model that generates answers grounded in the retrieved text.

Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) combines a retriever that finds relevant documents, usually via embeddings and a vector index, with a language model that generates answers grounded in the retrieved text.
Semantic search retrieves documents by meaning rather than exact keywords, by encoding queries and documents as dense embeddings and ranking them by vector similarity.
A vector database stores high-dimensional embedding vectors and serves fast approximate nearest-neighbour similarity queries over them.
Fine-tuning adapts a pretrained machine learning model to a specific task or domain by continuing training on task data, often with parameter-efficient methods.
Data science applies statistics, programming and machine learning to extract insight and build predictive models from data.
Data analysis is inspecting, cleaning, transforming and summarizing data to answer business questions, typically with SQL, spreadsheets, BI tools or pandas.
Data engineering is designing and operating pipelines and storage systems that ingest, transform and serve data reliably at scale for analytics and machine learning.
ETL (extract, transform, load) is the process of extracting data from source systems, transforming it and loading it into a target store such as a data warehouse.
A data pipeline is an automated sequence of steps that moves and transforms data between systems on a schedule or as a stream.
A data warehouse is a central analytical database that integrates cleaned historical data from many sources, modelled for reporting and OLAP queries.
A data lake is a storage repository that holds large volumes of raw structured and unstructured data in open file formats for later processing.
Big data engineering is processing datasets too large for a single machine using distributed frameworks such as Hadoop, Spark and streaming platforms.
Data modeling is designing the structure of data, including entities, relationships, keys and normalization, for databases and warehouses.
DevOps is the practice of automating how software is built, tested, released and operated, combining CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure as code, containers and monitoring.
CI/CD (continuous integration and continuous delivery or deployment) automates building, testing and releasing code on every change through pipelines.
Kubernetes is a container orchestration platform that schedules, scales and manages containerized workloads across a cluster of machines.
Docker is a containerization platform for packaging applications and their dependencies into portable images that run as isolated containers.
Containerization packages software with its dependencies into lightweight, isolated containers that run consistently across environments.
Container orchestration automates deployment, scaling, networking and healing of containers across a cluster.
Infrastructure as code manages servers, networks and cloud resources through versioned declarative configuration instead of manual setup.
Linux administration and development covers working with Linux distributions, the shell, services, permissions and system configuration.
Cloud computing is building and running systems on on-demand infrastructure and managed services from providers such as AWS, Azure or Google Cloud.
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is a cloud platform offering compute, storage, database, networking and managed services such as EC2, S3, Lambda and RDS.
Microsoft Azure is a cloud platform offering compute, storage, databases, identity and managed services such as AKS, Cosmos DB and Azure Functions.
Google Cloud Platform (GCP) is a cloud platform offering compute, data and machine learning services such as BigQuery, Cloud Run, GKE and Vertex AI.
Serverless computing runs application code in managed, event-driven functions or containers that scale automatically without managing servers.
Backend development is building the server-side part of applications: APIs, business logic, data access, authentication and integration with databases and queues.
Frontend development is building the client-side user interface of web applications with JavaScript frameworks, HTML and CSS, including state management and responsive layouts.
Web development is building websites and web applications, spanning browser-side interfaces and server-side APIs.
Mobile development is building native or cross-platform applications for iOS and Android devices.
REST API development is designing and implementing HTTP APIs that expose resources through standard methods, status codes and JSON payloads.
Microservices architecture structures an application as small, independently deployable services that communicate over APIs or message queues.
Database skills cover designing schemas, writing queries and operating relational or NoSQL database systems.
Relational databases store data in tables with keys and constraints and are queried with SQL; the skill covers schema design, joins, transactions and indexing.
NoSQL databases store data in non-relational models such as documents, key-value pairs, wide columns or graphs.
SQL is the query language for relational databases, used to select, join, aggregate and modify data and define schemas.
Software testing is verifying that code behaves correctly through automated unit, integration and end-to-end tests and structured test plans.
Unit testing is writing automated tests that verify individual functions or classes in isolation, often with mocks.
End-to-end testing automates real user flows through a running application, usually by driving a browser.
Load testing measures how a system behaves under expected and peak traffic by simulating many concurrent users or requests.
Performance testing evaluates latency, throughput and resource use of software under load to find bottlenecks.
Security testing looks for vulnerabilities in applications and infrastructure through scanning, code analysis and penetration tests.
Cybersecurity is protecting systems, networks and data from attacks through threat detection, vulnerability management, incident response and secure configuration.
Penetration testing is authorized simulated attacks on systems to find and exploit vulnerabilities before real attackers do.
Authentication is verifying user or service identity, using protocols and mechanisms such as OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, SAML, JWTs, SSO and multi-factor authentication.
Authorization is controlling what an authenticated user or service may do, using models such as role-based or attribute-based access control and policy engines.
Encryption protects data confidentiality by transforming it with cryptographic algorithms and managing the keys needed to decrypt it.
SIEM (security information and event management) platforms aggregate and correlate security logs to detect and investigate threats.
Technical compliance is implementing and evidencing controls required by security and privacy frameworks and regulations.
Observability is instrumenting systems with metrics, logs and traces so engineers can understand and debug their behaviour in production.
Infrastructure and application monitoring is collecting metrics and alerts about system health so problems are detected and resolved quickly.
The ELK stack combines Elasticsearch, Logstash and Kibana to collect, index, search and visualize logs.
Platform engineering builds internal developer platforms that give product teams self-service infrastructure, deployment and tooling.
Agile is an iterative way of delivering software in short cycles with continuous feedback, commonly using Scrum or Kanban ceremonies and artifacts.
Scrum is an agile framework that organizes work into fixed-length sprints with defined roles and ceremonies.
Project management is planning, scheduling, budgeting and coordinating work and stakeholders so a project delivers its scope on time.
Technical leadership is guiding a team's direction and delivery: leading engineers, mentoring, making decisions and owning outcomes.
Python is a general-purpose programming language widely used for web backends, data processing, automation and machine learning.
JavaScript is the programming language of the web, used for browser interfaces and, through Node.js, for servers and tooling.
Java is a statically typed, object-oriented programming language running on the JVM, widely used for enterprise backends and Android.
C# is a statically typed programming language on the .NET platform used for web backends, desktop applications and games.
